marks.gloss_en: ומאי רבי מאיר? דתניא: לא תצא אשה במפתח שבידה, ואם יצאת חייבת חטאת, דברי רבי מאיר; רבי אליעזר פוטר בכובלת ובצלוחית של פלייטון (kind tanya_kevatei: no kind names a bare דתניא)
R' Meir: a woman may not go out with a key in her hand, and if she went out she is liable to a sin-offering
זאת אומרת ... דהא אין בה בושם כפחות מכשיעור בכלי דמי, וקתני חייבת -- the baraita makes her liable for an empty perfume vessel, which is like less than a measure of food in a vessel
Rav Adda bar Ahava: that is to say, one who carries out less than the measure of food in a vessel is liable
בעלמא אימא לך פטור, ושאני הכא דליתיה לממשא כלל -- in general I can say he is exempt; the empty vessel differs, for there is no substance in it at all (= p_shani_hacha_leita_lemamasha)
Rav Ashi: here it is different, for there is no substance at all
כובלת מאן דכר שמה? -- R' Meir spoke of a key; who mentioned a kovelet, that R' Eliezer should exempt it?
חסורי מחסרא והכי קתני: וכן בכובלת וכן בצלוחית של פלייטון לא תצא ... דברי רבי מאיר; רבי אליעזר פוטר ... (= p_chasorei_mechasra, p_rm_tzlochit_chayevet)
the stam: [the baraita] is lacking [words], and this is what it teaches
כתיב הכא ״ושפח״ וכתיב התם ״לשאת ולספחת״ (Lev 14:56) -- the scab of Isa 3:17 is the sapachat listed among the forms of leprosy
R' Yosei b. R' Chanina: 'and the Lord will smite with a scab the crown of the daughters of Zion' (Isa 3:17) teaches that leprosy broke out among them
כדדריש רבה בר עולא: והיה תחת בשם מק יהיה -- the place they perfumed became rotting sores
ותחת חגורה נקפה -- the place of the sash became bruises
ותחת מעשה מקשה קרחה -- the place they adorned became bald patches
ותחת פתיגיל מחגרת שק -- the openings of pleasure became for sackcloth
the Gemara: what was their punishment?
Rava b. Rav Ilai: 'because the daughters of Zion are haughty' (Isa 3:16) -- they would walk with upright stature
one [of Rav and Shmuel]: 'and the Lord will lay bare their pot'hen' -- they were poured out like a jug

Rav: the people of Jerusalem were people of arrogance -- a man would say to his fellow: on what did you dine today? on kneaded bread or unkneaded? on white wine or dark? on a wide couch or a narrow one? with a good companion or a bad one?
הכי נמי דאסיר? והא רבה בר רב הונא איקלע לבי ריש גלותא ואישתי בקנישקנין ולא אמר ליה ולא מידי -- a pleasure the verse names was not forbidden (kind svara: no support kind names a ma'aseh)

ולטעמיך -- the same verse's mizrekei (kenishkanin) would then be forbidden too, yet Rabba bar Rav Huna said nothing when [the Exilarch] drank from them; אלא: the Rabbis decreed on pleasure with joy, not on pleasure without joy (= p_taanug_vesimcha_gazru, p_taanug_belo_simcha_lo_gazru)
'who drink in mizrekei of wine' (Amos 6:6): one said -- kenishkanin [many-spouted vessels]
מתיב רב יוסף: אף על פלייטון גזר רבי יהודה בן בבא ולא הודו לו; ואי אמרת משום תענוג, אמאי לא הודו לו? -- if the verse condemns palyaton for its pleasure, why did the Sages reject the decree on it?
R' Yehuda ben Bava decreed even on palyaton
Shmuel: 'and they anoint themselves with the chief of oils' (Amos 6:6) -- this is palyaton
Abaye: whatever has pleasure and has joy -- the Rabbis decreed on it
מגדף בה רבי אבהו: אי הכי, היינו דכתיב לכן עתה יגלו בראש גולים (Amos 6:7) -- because they urinate before their beds naked they shall go into exile at the head of the exiles?!
ולאו מלתא היא, דאמר רב חסדא: אנא משאי מלא חפני מיא ויהבו לי מלא חפני טיבותא -- that is not so: Rav Chisda's full handfuls of water brought full handfuls of good
Rav Chisda: I wash with full handfuls of water, and they gave me full handfuls of good
R' Yosei b. R' Chanina: 'and stretch [seruchim] upon their couches' (Amos 6:4) teaches that they would urinate before their beds naked
R' Abbahu: these are people who would eat and drink with one another, join their beds to one another, exchange their wives with one another, and foul their couches with seed not their own
three things bring a person to poverty: [first] one who urinates before his bed naked
Rava: we said this only where he turns his face toward his bed; [turned] outward, we have no problem with it
Rava, continuing: and where he turns toward his bed too, we said it only [when he urinates] onto the ground; into a vessel, we have no problem with it
Rava: [belittling handwashing] we said only where he does not wash his hands at all; washing and not [properly] washing, we have no problem with it
Rava: [the wife who curses him to his face] -- over the matter of her ornaments
